# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–23 (Complete – Updated 163)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: **Autumn of sixth year** (Chapter 23). Rawdon has discovered Rebecca with Steyne and confronted them; Rebecca remains in wreckage of their chamber as Rawdon departs, likely forever. Amelia continues evening vigils at Russell Square. Little Rawdon at school and progressing.
- **Key temporal markers**: Chapter 22 opened "summer of sixth year"; Chapter 23 opens "autumn of sixth year." Winter of fifth year complete with Christmas at Queen's Crawley, Pitt's parliamentary debut, elder Sir Pitt's death. Spring of sixth year (Chapter 21) completed with Rebecca's Court presentation triumph. Seasonal details: Frost silvered hedges overnight. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. Light went early as autumn advanced. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Children chased hoop down lane. Smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields.
- **Locations**: Salwick (bridge toll skimmed monthly); Harrowgate; Dunholt; Bryngate; Yarlton; Quenwick (river crossing); Dunwick (river crossing, forge with chalked sun, baker's boy late); London (Curzon Street, Great Gaunt Street, Piccadilly, St. James's Street, Russell Square, Baker Street, Hyde Park Ring, Levant House, Foundling Church, Gaunt House, Gaunt Square, Serpentine, Cursitor Street); Queen's Crawley; Court palace; Gulton; Mirecombe; Brookgreen Fair; Coldcombe; Fenmere; school in City; Astley's; May Fair; Chancery Lane; the Temple; Paddington.

## The Catastrophic Discovery (Chapters 22–23)

**Rawdon's Return Home (Chapter 22)**: After Lady Jane's rescue from spunging-house, Rawdon walked home rapidly at nine o'clock. Found drawing-room windows blazing with light. She had claimed illness prevented rescue attempt.

**The Confrontation (Chapter 22–23 transition)**
- Rawdon entered house silently, heard laughter and singing in upper rooms
- Found Steyne bowing to kiss Rebecca's hand
- Rebecca sat in brilliant full toilette, arms and fingers sparkling with bracelets and rings, brilliants on breast given by Steyne
- Rebecca screamed faintly; Steyne rose grinding teeth, pale with fury

**Rebecca's Denial and Rawdon's Rage (Chapter 23)**
- Rebecca claimed innocence: "I am innocent, Rawdon...before God, I am innocent"
- Rawdon screamed: "You innocent! Damn you...Every trinket you have on your body is paid for by me. I have given you thousands of pounds, which this fellow has spent and for which he has sold you...You're as innocent as your mother, the ballet-girl, and your husband the bully"
- **REVELATION**: Rebecca's mother was a ballet-girl; Rawdon's father was a bully

**Physical Confrontation (Chapter 23)**
- Steyne attempted to leave, asserting superiority
- Rawdon seized Steyne by neckcloth until nearly strangled; Steyne writhed and bent
- Rawdon struck Steyne twice over face with open hand, flung him bleeding to ground
- Steyne wore scar to his dying day
- Rebecca admired Rawdon: "strong, brave, and victorious"

**Destruction and Jewel Discovery (Chapter 23)**
- Rawdon ordered Rebecca: "Take off those things"
- Rebecca trembled, pulled jewels from arms and rings from fingers, held them in quivering heap
- Rawdon dropped them; tore diamond ornament from her breast, flung it at Steyne (cut his bald forehead)
- Rebecca gave all keys but one; one belonged to small desk Amelia had given her in early days, kept in secret place
- Rawdon flung open boxes and wardrobes, found the desk
- **Contents of desk**: Papers, love-letters many years old, trinkets, woman's memoranda, pocket-book with bank-notes
- **CRITICAL DISCOVERY**: Bank-notes dated back ten years; one fresh note for **one thousand pounds from Lord Steyne**
- **IMPLICATION**: Steyne had been financially supporting Rebecca extensively; this constitutes payment for sexual favors

**Rawdon's Departure and Stated Plans (Chapter 23)**
- Day had dawned; hours passed in search
- Rawdon stated: "I'll send it [the thousand pounds] to him to-day, and I will pay Briggs, who was kind to the boy, and some of the debts. You will let me know where I shall send the rest to you. You might have spared me a hundred pounds, Becky, out of all this--I have always shared with you"
- **Decision/Plan**: Use Steyne's money to pay debts, especially to Briggs; leave remainder for Rebecca
- **State**: Rawdon's tone bitter but resolved; accusation that she withheld hundred pounds when he needed it for spunging-house

**Rebecca's Aftermath (Chapter 23)**
- Remained for hours after Rawdon left, sunshine pouring into room
- Sat alone on bed's edge; drawers open, contents scattered
- Dresses, feathers, scarfs, trinkets in heap of tumbled vanities
- Hair falling over shoulders; gown torn where Rawdon wrenched brilliants
- Heard him go downstairs, door slamming and closing
- **Certainty**: "She knew he would never come back. He was gone forever"
- **Suicidal ideation**: "Would he kill himself?--she thought--not until after he had met Lord Steyne. She thought of her long past life, and all the dismal incidents of it. Ah, how dreary it seemed, how miserable, lonely and profitless! Should she take laudanum, and end it, to have done with all hopes, schemes, debts, and triumphs?"
- **French maid's response**: Found Rebecca in position of despair with clasped hands and dry eyes. Maid was "her accomplice and in Steyne's pay"
- **Recovery attempt**: Maid persuaded mistress to lie down on bed with "entreaty and show of kindness"
- **Aftermath**: Maid gathered up trinkets from floor where Rebecca had dropped them at Rawdon's orders

**State Change**: Rebecca's social ascendancy has culminated in complete financial and marital catastrophe. Her affair with Steyne, concealed only nominally, has been exposed. Rawdon has abandoned her permanently with stated intention to rebuild life through honest debt-payment. Rebecca faces ruin, scandal, and possible suicide.

## Amelia's Continued Separation and Maternal Anguish (Chapter 22)
- George departed to live with Old Osborne permanently; now visits on pony with coachman
- Child completely unaffected; adopted imperious air within two days
- Amelia takes evening walks to Russell Square when George does not visit; rests by garden railing opposite Osborne house
- Looks up at illuminated drawing-room windows; sees at nine o'clock chamber where Georgy sleeps
- Prays with humble heart as light goes out; walks home shrinking and silent, very tired
- Grows care-worn and sad; sleeps little; weeps and prays in long silent nights
- **State**: "He is not her boy any more"

## Little Rawdon at School (Chapter 22)
- Honest Briggs made up little kit; Rebecca would not allow carriage (cab used instead)
- Rebecca did not offer kiss; child did not propose to embrace her
- Rawdon walked home very dismally; dined alone with Briggs
- Very kind to Briggs, grateful for her love and watchfulness
- At school: Young Blackball made him fag, shoe-black, breakfast toaster; initiated him into Latin Grammar; thrashed him three or four times
- Rawdon visited and found lad sufficiently well and happy, grinning and laughing in black gown and breeches

## Rawdon's Prior Financial Crisis and Spunging-House (Chapter 22)

**Arrest and Detention**: Rawdon detained at Mr. Moss's mansion in Cursitor Street, Chancery Lane—a spunging-house. Debt to Nathan one-hundred-fifty, with costs one-hundred-seventy.

**Rebecca's Failure to Rescue (Chapter 22)**: Rawdon wrote letter asking Rebecca to bring money or arrangements. Day passed with no messenger, no Becky. Received beautiful, highly scented letter on pink paper with light green seal claiming she was ill, consulted Mr. Blench (doctor) who gave composing draught, visited Nathan who refused release without all money or imprisonment, found Steyne at house offering compliments, begged Steyne on knees for two hundred pounds which he promised to send in morning. **CLAIM/PLAN**: She cared and was distressed; longed to free him; Steyne promised money in morning. **REALITY**: Steyne's promise was false; he sent no money. Rebecca made no rescue attempt despite having opportunities.

**Lady Jane's Rescue (Chapter 22)**: Rawdon's note to Gaunt Street brought Lady Jane (Pitt was at parliamentary dinner). She came herself in cab, settled Mr. Moss's bills quickly. Rawdon overcame with emotion, ran to her, caught her in arms, sobbed on her shoulder. Jane beaming with happiness. Rawdon thanked her hundred times with ardour, said in rude artless way he was changed since knowing her and little Rawdy, wanted to change, did not finish sentence. That night Jane prayed humbly for poor way-worn sinner by her own little boy's bed.

## Key Relationships and Character States

**Rawdon's Transformation**: Through Lady Jane's kindness and his own paternal feelings, best and honestest feelings of man came out. Her rescue prompted reflection on need for change. His discovery of Rebecca's affair and financial corruption by Steyne has severed marriage permanently. His stated plan to use Steyne's own money to pay debts and especially Briggs (kind to little Rawdy) shows moral regeneration in process.

**Rebecca's Complete Collapse**: From social triumph to utter ruin in single night. Exposed as Steyne's paid mistress. Husband gone forever. Facing scandal and financial destitution. Accomplice maid (in Steyne's pay) her only comfort. Suicidal despair. No path to recovery visible.

**Steyne's Humiliation**: Exposed as financial corruptor and seducer. Scarred by diamond ornament flung at him; wore scar to dying day. Forced to retreat in shame before Rawdon's violence.

**Amelia's Continued Anguish**: Separated from son permanently; son indifferent to separation; mother's daily ritual of longing and prayer continues; no resolution in sight.

## Minor Characters and Details
- **Rebecca's mother**: Ballet-girl (revelation in Rawdon's rage)
- **Rebecca's father (Rawdon's characterization)**: Bully
- **Briggs**: Remains kind to little Rawdon; will receive payment from Rawdon using Steyne's money
- **French maid (Finette)**: Rebecca's accomplice, in Steyne's pay; persuaded Rebecca toward recovery
- **Mr. Moss, Captain Walker, Miss Moss, Mrs. Moss**: As previously documented
- **Unnamed characters in autumn settings**: Ilzek Wexwood, Daena Wexwood, Eldette, Ridette Lindson, Jotho, Feten, Nyrine, Jolia, Thidrek Corrett, Manelle Corrett, Jolia Corrett
